title: Granular isolation ledger and burst consent — PRD draft
content:
Context:

This is a working PRD for a proposal that combines a tenant-level isolation ledger (tracking isolation credits and historical isolation events) with an opt-in 'burst consent' mechanism that lets tenants explicitly accept temporary isolation-relaxed executions in exchange for improved availability or lower cost. The goal is to provide predictable, auditable isolation behavior while unlocking safer opportunistic capacity for tenants that want it.

Why this is different: most prior proposals focus on autoscale heuristics, headroom, or fallback lanes. This introduces an auditable accounting layer (ledger) and an explicit tenant consent model so we can surface trade-offs to customers and attach billing/credits/policy to burst events.

Goals (MVP):
- Define an isolation ledger schema and API for recording: isolation credits balance, granted temporary-relaxations, eviction events, fallback model variants, and reason codes.
- Implement a simple burst consent flag per tenant with 3 modes: "opt-out", "opt-in best-effort", "opt-in guaranteed-burst".
- Integrate consent with routing so that requests from opt-in tenants can be routed to opportunistic pools when Dedicated pools are constrained.
- Emit telemetry and audit trails for every ledger entry and every burst event for debugging, billing, and compliance.
- Provide a console view (table + timeline) showing ledger history and current credit balance.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Full marketplace for buying/reselling headroom credits (future phase).
- Complex auctioning between tenants for burst spots.
- On-prem private control-plane implementation — start hosted/Dedicated only.

User problems / stories:
- Platform engineer at a high-growth startup wants to reduce 5xxs during peak while retaining strict isolation for most traffic. They want an auditable way to see when their traffic was permitted to run on opportunistic capacity and the cost impact.
- SRE wants an ops knob to temporarily relax isolation for low-priority batch jobs to protect tail latency of high-priority routes.
- Billing and procurement needs a trail to reconcile when a tenant consumed burst capacity so they can be charged or debited from credits.

Assumptions:
- We have existing fallback routing machinery that can send requests to compatible model variants or lower-fidelity quantized models.
- Opportunistic pools are available within the same region and can run compatible model binaries.
- Token-level accounting and request attribution already exist in infra.

High-level design:
1) Isolation Ledger service (lightweight, append-only):
   - records events: CREDIT_ISSUED, CREDIT_CONSUMED, BURST_GRANTED, BURST_REJECTED, FALLBACK_REROUTE, EVICTION, MANUAL_ADJUST.
   - fields (flat key-value): tenant_id, event_time, event_type, amount (tokens/credits), reason_code, effective_window, routing_target_id, operator_id, linked_request_ids
   - ledger is the single source of truth for current isolation credit balance and last N events for console.

2) Burst Consent modes (tenant-level config):
   - opt-out (default): never route to opportunistic capacity.
   - opt-in best-effort: allow routing to opportunistic capacity when Dedicated pool is overwhelmed; no SLA guarantees; lower cost.
   - opt-in guaranteed-burst (paid/credit-backed): commit to paying for reserved burst capacity or spend credits; platform will prioritize these requests ahead of best-effort.

3) Router integration:
   - policy check at routing decision time: check tenant consent mode + ledger balance + pool health signals.
   - if allowed, issue a BURST_GRANTED event to ledger and attach a burst_session_id to request trace.
   - implement soft quota: a tenant cannot consume more than X% of allowed burst credits per rolling window unless explicitly approved.

4) Billing/credits:
   - credits can be issued by ops, by reserved burst purchase, or auto-granted in limited promos.
   - credits are consumed at the time of BURST_GRANTED. The ledger stores pre/post balances for reconciliation.

5) Console/UX:
   - Tenant settings page: consent mode toggle, current credit balance, recent ledger events, button to 'buy burst credits' (links to billing flow).
   - Per-route latency and burst exposure graph (stacked timeline of when requests were run on opportunistic vs dedicated pools).

Telemetry and observability:
- Emit structured events to existing tracing and metrics: burst_request_count, burst_granted_count, burst_rejected_count, avg_latency_opportunistic, avg_latency_dedicated, burst_credit_balance (gauge).
- Audit logs: every ledger write is replicated to append-store and available via console and export (CSV).
- Alerting: sudden depletion of credits, spike in BURST_REJECTED, or if opportunistic pool tail latency breaches threshold.

Operational runbook (short):
- Detection: SRE gets alert for spike in burst_rejected_count -> check ledger for tenants with high demand.
- Mitigation: temporarily increase global soft-burst-capacity or move warm pool capacity.
- Customer comms: notify affected tenants and optionally issue complimentary credits if SLA breach suspected.

Security & compliance considerations:
- Ledger entries are PII-free (tenant_id only), but must be stored with access controls and audit history.
- For regulated customers we will default to opt-out; opt-in guaranteed-burst requires explicit contractual acknowledgment.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Credit currency definition: should credits be time-based (minutes of GPU time), token-based (per-token cost multiplier), or request-weighted? (TODO: run 2-week simulation using historical traces).
- Q2: Preemption semantics: when an opportunistic task is preempted, do we refund credits partially? (proposal: prorated refund for unused time window).
- Q3: Compatibility matching: how strict should model variant compatibility be for routing to opportunistic pools? (TODO: define compatibility matrix).
- Q4: UI limits: how many ledger events do we surface in console without pagination?

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (experiments): implement ledger write-only integration for 2 test tenants to validate event model and telemetry (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (alpha): enable opt-in best-effort for internal beta tenants; route a small percentage of traffic to opportunistic pools; expose console view (6 weeks).
- Phase 2 (paid beta): enable opt-in guaranteed-burst with credits purchase flow; integrate billing; expand to limited customers (8–12 weeks).
- Phase 3 (GA): enable full self-serve burst purchase, SLO SLAs for guaranteed-burst, and add marketplace features (Q3+).

Success metrics (initial):
- Latency 95th percentile reduction for affected high-volume tenants during peak vs baseline.
- Number of tenants actively using opt-in modes.
- Accuracy of ledger: 100% event replication with reconciliation discrepancy <0.01% after 30 days.
- Billing reconciliation errors <0.1% at month boundary.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Tenants accidentally opt-in and experience lower isolation -> mitigation: clear UI copy, consent flow, and default opt-out.
- Risk: Complexity of reconciling credits -> mitigation: ledger is append-only with checksums and nightly reconciliation job.
- Risk: Opportunistic pool misconfiguration leads to incorrect model serving -> mitigation: compatibility matrix and canarying of models to opportunistic pools.

Appendix / references:
- Related internal docs: 'predictive-warm-pool-orchestrator' (see linked artifacts), 'burst-credit-allocator' (historical notes).
- Slack threads: #dedicated-capacity discussion 2025-11-20: "burst consent edge cases".

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight — feedback requested on credit currency preference and preemption refund semantics.
- Please add specific telemetry keys you need for billing in the comments below or link Jira tickets to DED-9821.

Quick TODOs (owner: Aisha):

- [ ] Prototype ledger write API and sample event schema (eng-serving-runtime)

- [ ] Draft pricing proposal for guaranteed-burst

-- end of draft (working doc)
